standard.title: Stereotypes and choices
standard.description: describe how choices and actions can be influenced by stereotypes
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have described their personal qualities and those of others, and explained how they contribute to developing identities (AC9HP2P01). They have a basic understanding of personal qualities but have not yet examined how external stereotypes influence choices and actions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students describe how choices and actions can be influenced by stereotypes.

nodes.label: Stereotypes in texts and media
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify gender stereotypes in texts and media and discuss the messages they portray and how they can influence choices and actions.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one stereotype in a text or media example and describe the message it sends about what is expected of a particular group.
nodes.typical_width: Explore a range of texts and media examples; identify stereotypes about gender and other characteristics; discuss the messages portrayed and how they could influence a person's choices or actions.
wider: Analyse how stereotypes in media targeting children (advertisements, games, toys, clothing) send messages about what is 'for' which gender, and investigate how these messages may limit choices.
Compare stereotyping in media across two different time periods or cultural contexts, examining how portrayals have changed or remained similar.
nodes.hinge_reason: Recognising a stereotype as a message about expected behaviour is the prerequisite conceptual move. Students who cannot identify a stereotype as such cannot describe how it influences choices — they will describe the influence without identifying its source.

response_modes.reason: Students need a working definition of 'stereotype' and practice identifying examples before they can analyse influence. A define-identify-analyse sequence with concrete media examples is more effective than abstract discussion of the concept.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one stereotype in a text or media example.
Describes the message the stereotype sends about a particular group.
Explains how that message could influence a person's choices or actions.

nodes.label: Unfair treatment and human rights
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise that unfair or unequal treatment based on gender, abilities or other differences is wrong and against human rights.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe what unfair or unequal treatment means in a school or community context, and connect it to the idea that all people deserve to be treated fairly.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss how stereotypes can lead to unfair treatment of people based on gender, abilities or other characteristics; connect this to the concept of human rights and equal treatment.
wider: Investigate a specific human rights principle (e.g. the right to education, the right to be treated without discrimination) and examine how stereotypes can threaten this right.
Explore examples from history or current events where unfair treatment based on stereotypes was challenged, and discuss what changed as a result.

response_modes.reason: Connecting stereotype-based treatment to human rights requires an explicit conceptual bridge. Students need to understand that rights are not just about rules — they are about the equal worth of people — before the 'unfair' judgement has moral grounding.

success_criteria: Describes what unfair treatment looks like in a familiar context.
Explains why treating people unequally based on stereotypes is wrong.
Uses the term 'human rights' correctly in their explanation.

nodes.label: Fair and equitable roles and responsibilities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe ways to make roles and responsibilities at home, at school and in communities fair, equitable and inclusive.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one situation where roles or responsibilities are distributed unequally based on stereotypes, and suggest a more equitable approach.
nodes.typical_width: Describe how stereotypes influence role and responsibility distribution across home, school and community contexts; identify specific actions that promote fairness and equity in each.
wider: Design an audit of roles and responsibilities in a familiar context (e.g. classroom tasks, household jobs) to identify where stereotyping is influencing distribution, and propose a fairer system.
Explore how stereotyped expectations about gender roles in physical activity limit participation for some students and discuss what schools and communities can do to address this.

response_modes.reason: Stereotyped role distribution looks different at home, school and community levels. Students who only explore one context have limited understanding of how pervasive and varied the influence of stereotypes can be.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Exploring stereotyped role expectations across multiple contexts (home chores, classroom roles, sport, community leadership) builds significantly richer understanding of how stereotypes shape everyday choices — each context offers a distinct and meaningful lens.
success_criteria: Identifies at least one context where roles or responsibilities are affected by stereotypes.
Proposes a specific change that would make the distribution fairer.
Practises or demonstrates a way to challenge a stereotyped expectation.
